Pakistan’s education system fails youth as skills crisis costs economy $31.5 billion annually Pakistan’s worsening skills crisis and persistent unemployment among educated youth have exposed serious shortcomings in the country’s education and employment systems, with inadequate vocational training reportedly costing the economy billions of dollars annually, as reported by Dawn. Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Pakistan’s worsening skills crisis and persistent unemployment among educated youth have exposed serious shortcomings in the country’s education and employment systems, with inadequate vocational training reportedly costing the economy billions of dollars annually, as reported by Dawn. According to Dawn, only seven per cent of Pakistani youth receive formal technical and vocational training, significantly below the regional average of 22 per cent. World Bank estimates suggest that this skills deficit results in annual economic losses of approximately USD 31.5 billion through reduced productivity and missed export opportunities. The alarming situation has brought Pakistan’s employment challenges into focus at the World Economic Forum’s annual Global Future Leaders meeting. Discussions examining youth employment in the age of artificial intelligence have highlighted Pakistan as an example of the growing disconnect between educational qualifications and labour market requirements. Nearly one-third of Pakistanis aged between 15 and 29 are neither employed nor pursuing education or training. The situation is particularly concerning for young women, more than half of whom fall into this category, reflecting substantial barriers to economic participation. Experts attribute the crisis to longstanding institutional weaknesses rather than inadequate capabilities among young Pakistanis. Limited access to professional mentorship, career counselling, industry connections and reliable employment information has prevented qualified individuals from securing suitable opportunities. Unemployment among graduates has reached 18.3 per cent, surpassing the overall unemployment rate of 14.7 per cent. These figures reveal a troubling contradiction in Pakistan’s education system, where higher academic qualifications do not necessarily translate into improved employment prospects, as highlighted by Dawn. The situation is particularly difficult among younger university graduates. Citing Gallup Pakistan’s assessment of the Labour Force Survey 2024-25, unemployment among graduates aged 20 to 24 stands at 32.8 per cent. With nearly one in three young graduates struggling to find employment, Pakistan faces mounting pressure to reform its education-to-employment framework, as reported by Dawn. (ANI)

item.title: ‘The X-Files’ returns! Ryan Coogler’s reboot to feature new FBI agents
item.description: Deadwyler and Patel will be seen in new characters instead of iterations of Gillian Anderson’s Dana Scully and David Duchovny’s Fox Mulder.
item.content:encoded:
‘The X-Files’ returns! Ryan Coogler’s reboot to feature new FBI agents Deadwyler and Patel will be seen in new characters instead of iterations of Gillian Anderson’s Dana Scully and David Duchovny’s Fox Mulder. ANI | Updated: 14-10-2026 14:11 IST | Created: 14-10-2026 14:11 IST

Filmmaker Ryan Coogler (File photo/Reuters) . Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Filmmaker Ryan Coogler’s ‘X-Files’ reboot is all set to get started! A reimagining of the 1990s sci-fi drama, the show will feature Danielle Deadwyler and Hinesh Patel as “two highly decorated but vastly different FBI agents who form an unlikely bond when they are assigned to a long-shuttered division devoted to cases involving unexplained phenomena,” as per the official synopsis, Variety reported. According to a source, Deadwyler and Patel will be seen in new characters instead of iterations of Gillian Anderson’s Dana Scully and David Duchovny’s Fox Mulder. The show, which was picked up by Hulu in February, has been written, directed, and executive produced by Ryan Coogler. The Oscar-winning filmmaker will also serve as executive producer of the series alongside showrunner Jennifer Yale. “I’ve loved ‘The X-Files’ for a long time, so getting the chance to write and direct the pilot has meant a great deal to me. What Chris Carter created is special, and we wanted to honour everything that made the original series connect with so many people while also finding our own way into that world. Danielle and Himesh, along with the rest of our cast, have brought such original perspectives and performances to these characters, and watching that come together has been one of the most rewarding parts of the experience,” Coogler said, as quoted by Variety. The upcoming ‘X-Files’ is produced by Proximity Media, which Coogler co-founded with Zinzi Coogler and Sev Ohanian, as well as 20th Television. The original ‘X-Files’ ran for 11 seasons in total on Fox, earning 61 Emmy nominations and 15 wins. It went on to become a sci-fi touchstone with vast influence on television and pop culture. (ANI)
